After years of working in libraries I organize my shelves by the good old Dewey decimal system.
By genre. Topleft= favorites. Afterwards alphabetic. Series in order, alphabetic. Bottom shelf= unsorted mess I still need to read
Factual books by subject and sub-subject, fiction by genre, than in all cases alphabetically by author.
I have one room for fiction/video games and another for non-fiction/comics.

One book case for novels of fiction. Two that are assorted historical volumes - mostly classical antiquity on the bottom, dark ages/middle ages above that, Renaissance/Revolution above that, then the Victorian era 'til WW2 above that. I also have a bookshelf for programming, cooking, woodworking, gardening and various other trade skills.
Big books are on the largest shelf. The rest are in no order but some authors are grouped together.
By genre, and alphabetically within each section. I have a lot of books, mostly paperback, but with a few decent hard-covers I got as gifts.

The main collection, a mix of literary fiction and science fiction / fantasy, is alphabetical by author and roughly chronological or haphazard for each author.
